title: GPT-4o’s gender associations for inattentive ADHD changed with cue wording
summary: In a controlled association task, female-associated responses for inattentive ADHD prompts fell from 80.4% with explicit gender categories to 38.5% with implicitly gendered names. The study measures GPT-4o’s choices under these prompt conditions. It did not test patient diagnosis or estimate ADHD prevalence.

source_review.scope: v1 cue-list methods, reference sample notes and Study 1 results

evidence.tested: The study compared explicit and name-based cue lists on researcher-written contexts, including a control category and an auxiliary clinical-sample proxy.
evidence.unknown: Effects may depend on the model, names and prompts. The clinical sample is selective and cannot establish true population prevalence.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4o assigned gendered associations to research prompts using differently expressed cues under a Context Association Test.
